newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar presidential poll to be held November 3.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar presidential poll to be held November 3.

text.p: Madagascar will hold presidential elections on November 3 following last week's impeachment of President Albert Zafy, the government announced in a statement on Wednesday night.
Political parties and presidential candidates would be allowed to campaign from October 13 to November 2, parliamentary officials in the Indian Ocean island said.
Zafy, 69, was impeached last week for violating the constitution. He was replaced by interim president Norbert Ratsirahonana until the election within two months.
Zafy had warned the interim leadership of trouble if they did not hold the elections within the short time frame. He has said he will run in the poll again and hopes to regain power.
Parliament had invoked what it said were Zafy's repeated violations of the constitution and accused him of acting against the interests of the people.
The crisis was a result of growing opposition to Zafy, who won Madagascar's multi-party elections in 1993, defeating former military ruler Didier Ratsiraka after 17 years in power.
